findings.scope: Two propagated proof loci, one finding. The final strong-generator and coherent-sheaf boundedness statements remain valid.

findings.original: For an arbitrary countable factorization, u_n beta_n is claimed zero by construction; this is used to assert that the telescope map acts as the identity.
findings.adverse_evidence: D(k), E all shifts of k, H=Hom(-,k), and the X_1 summand indexed by id_k give theta_2(u_1 beta_1)=id_k. Thus u_1 beta_1 is nonzero and t alpha is not alpha.
findings.correction: Prove the restricted Yoneda countable-coproduct comparison by evaluation presentations. Split the restricted tower from its second stage into its common quotient and killed kernels, construct the finite-prefix left inverse, and retain the initial stage by an explicit target automorphism.
findings.limits: The source theorem and its hypotheses remain valid. The retraction is a natural transformation on the restricted category, not a claimed splitting of the telescope morphism in D.

findings.original: A and B are arbitrary subcategories; degree-zero orthogonality and a decomposition triangle for every object are asserted equivalent to an admissible pair.
findings.adverse_evidence: In D^b(k), D^{<=0}(k) and D^{>=1}(k) satisfy the displayed decomposition using the actual truncation subcomplex and quotient. They are not invariant under both shifts and are not triangulated. Fullness also cannot be inferred from an objectwise condition using ambient Hom.
findings.correction: Require strictly full subcategories invariant under all shifts, then prove that (3) gives B=A-perp and A=left-perp-B. Their saturated triangulated structures follow, so the adjoint criteria apply.
findings.limits: Cone closure is proved, not added as an unnecessary premise. The quotient and adjoint conclusions survive under the corrected exact hypotheses.

findings.original: Any one of three conditions implies at most one morphism of Postnikov systems.
findings.adverse_evidence: An explicit length-three pair in D^b(k) has both terminal objects zero, so conditions (1) and (2) hold, but admits two maps over the zero complex map with different nonzero intermediate h.
findings.correction: All three conditions imply terminal-map uniqueness; condition (3) additionally implies uniqueness of the whole map of systems.
findings.limits: This is a uniqueness correction, not a new existence statement.

findings.original: After splitting the two outer essentially constant systems, the proof invokes TR3 for a projection triangle map at the first index.
findings.adverse_evidence: In D^b(k), the first triangle k->0->k[1]->k[1] with identity boundary has no comparison to k->k->0 inducing identity on k; all subsequent identity triangles do.
findings.correction: Compute both off-diagonal blocks. Constant-to-pro-zero vanishes at every index; pro-zero-to-constant vanishes only on a further tail. Take that tail before applying TR3.
findings.limits: The statement and all hypotheses survive. The error is in the unconditional first-index projection claim, not in essential constancy of the middle system.

claims.original_statement: Zero-endpoint endomorphisms of one distinguished triangle have pairwise zero product; five Hom-vanishing conditions guarantee uniqueness.
claims.proved_statement: For any two distinguished triangles, middle components with zero endpoints form the explicit intersection of two factorization-image subgroups. These groups form a square-zero ideal across all distinguished triangles. Completion sets are torsors for these groups, with the stated exact inverse formula.
claims.hypotheses: Pre-triangulated category; original shift comparisons retained; no TR4 needed.
claims.completed_propagation: Opening idempotent polynomial and exact uniqueness criterion proved.
claims.unresolved_propagation: Check later derived idempotent-completion and orthogonality uses and the receiving perfect/equiv passages during ordered review.

claims.original_statement: Countable products or coproducts make a pre-triangulated category Karoubian; the existing Verdier functorial-cone lemma uses that sufficient hypothesis.
claims.proved_statement: A countable power of a single object suffices to split its idempotents. Powers for every object suffice globally; dually for copowers. The functorial-cone decomposition only requires the category to be Karoubian, with the exact kernel constructed from the source section.
claims.completed_propagation: Exact Phi/Psi coordinates, complementary kernels and Verdier receiving kernel maps proved; insertion preserved.
claims.unresolved_propagation: Any additional use later in this chapter or other chapters is checked separately, not inferred from this local strengthening.

claims.original_statement: An adjoint of an exact functor between triangulated categories is exact; a fully faithful exact functor with an exact right adjoint of zero kernel is an equivalence.
claims.proved_statement: Both results hold between pre-triangulated categories. The right adjoint acquires the explicitly constructed exact shift comparison, and unit and counit satisfy the proved compatibility equations. Separate exactness of the right adjoint is unnecessary in the equivalence test.
claims.hypotheses: Original additive categories, TR1-TR3, exact F, adjunction F left adjoint to G; full faithfulness and zero kernel only for the equivalence assertion.

claims.original_statement: Totalization and fixed-factor tensor totalization are exact when the target additive category has countable direct sums.
claims.proved_statement: For either outer-complex convention, double complexes whose diagonal coproducts exist form a full triangulated subcategory, and Tot on it is exact with the original comparison. Fixed-factor tensor functors are exact on their corresponding domains; same-side bounded factors require only finite biproducts.
claims.hypotheses: Additive categories, original commuting double-complex differentials, the specified diagonal coproducts, and bilinearity for tensor products. No strict-fullness or automatic existence from homotopy equivalence is asserted.
claims.propagation: Exact component comparisons checked; existing tensor source conclusions unchanged.

claims.original_statement: A sequence of chain maps with the listed staggered cohomology vanishings factors through a lower truncation; dual assertion included.
claims.proved_statement: The factorization holds for arbitrary derived morphisms with any integer initial cutoff b and target cutoff b-n. If final cohomology vanishes below a and n>b-a, the composite is zero. The ideal of cohomologically zero endomorphisms of an object of amplitude [a,b] has power b-a+1 equal to zero, with the complete finite inverse for 1-u.
claims.hypotheses: Abelian category; source upper bound, the exact staggered vanishing maps, and final lower bound only for zero composition. No intermediate boundedness or homological-dimension hypothesis.
claims.propagation: All five direct uses checked for this implication. More Algebra target repaired; existing constants retained, and c(t+1) supplies the local annihilation step.

claims.original_statement: The source assumes D-prime Karoubian to infer existence of RF(X) and RF(Y) from RF(X direct-sum Y).
claims.proved_statement: If V=RF(X direct-sum Y), RF(X) exists exactly when e=RF(i_X p_X) on V splits. The Y criterion uses 1-e. In the triangulated target either splitting produces the complementary splitting by the explicit triangle construction, so either criterion gives both values. The same assertions hold for LF.
claims.hypotheses: The original exact F, saturated compatible S, triangulated target, and an existing value on the specified direct sum. No global Karoubian assumption is required for the criterion.
claims.propagation: Product cofinality proved; local splitting criterion proved in both variances; domain summand closure characterized; computing-object receiver proved with actual F(X),F(Y) splittings.

claims.original_statement: A bounded-below complex of right F-acyclic objects computes RF when RF is defined there.
claims.proved_statement: If only terms through q are right F-acyclic, the canonical comparison is an isomorphism below q and monic in degree q. Its cokernel is im(delta_F) intersect ker(H^(q+1)(eta_T)) for the original-term tail T=sigma_(>=q+1)A. If F is left exact this defect is zero, so the comparison is also an isomorphism in degree q.
claims.hypotheses: Original bounded-below complex A, the given defined RF(A), and acyclicity of the stated finite prefix. The last assertion additionally assumes left exactness. The differential into A^(q+1) is retained.
claims.propagation: The full Leray statement follows degree by degree. Its acyclic special case repairs enough-acyclics; the finite-prefix refinement is applied to the actual global-sections complex with its outgoing differential retained. Perfect receives a separate exact truncation repair.

claims.original_statement: Under the Serre epimorphism-lifting hypothesis, D^-(B) maps equivalently to D^-_B(A).
claims.proved_statement: The quasi-isomorphic B-term subcomplexes of a fixed bounded-above X with B-cohomology form a filtered poset. Finite families of chain maps and chosen homotopies from B-complexes factor through one such subcomplex; the exact Hom_K colimit formula follows. The comparison restricts to D^b and preserves all derived-category Ext groups and their products.
claims.hypotheses: Exactly the original Serre epimorphism-lifting hypothesis, bounded-above X with B-cohomology, and bounded-above B-complexes as sources of the retained maps and homotopies.
claims.existing_overlap: The bounded restriction already appears in the receiving Perfect proposition; no claim that it was absent from the corpus.

claims.original_statement: A quasi-isomorphism induces an isomorphism on homotopy classes into a bounded-below injective complex; monomorphic quasi-isomorphisms allow strict lifts, unique up to homotopy.
claims.proved_statement: For I^n=0 below a with injective terms, cohomology isomorphisms only in degrees n>=a suffice for the Hom comparison. A termwise monomorphism satisfying this range permits strict lifts, and two strict lifts have a homotopy vanishing on the original subcomplex. The explicit degree-reversing dual gives the projective version with n<=b and homotopies killed by the quotient map.
claims.hypotheses: The actual target I, its lower term bound a and injective terms; the displayed cohomology range for the actual map. Strict statements additionally use its degreewise monomorphisms. Dual bounds and epimorphisms are explicitly proved.

claims.original_statement: A short exact sequence of bounded-below complexes has a compatible sequence of injective resolutions in which the first resolution may be prescribed.
claims.proved_statement: Both outer injective resolutions may be prescribed, without requiring the given right-hand resolution map to be monic. A homotopy gives the upper-right entry h in the actual middle map [[1,h],[0,f_3]]. The explicitly computed projective dual retains both prescribed outer projective resolutions. Existing common term bounds are preserved.
claims.hypotheses: The source short exact sequence and the two actually given bounded outer resolutions. No extra enough-injectives/projectives hypothesis is needed once those resolutions are supplied.

claims.original_statement: Two Cartan-Eilenberg spectral sequences and the derived-composition criterion are stated for left exact functors.
claims.proved_statement: Given a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution, both spectral sequences work for additive F. With enough injectives, the composition criterion and Grothendieck sequence work for additive F,G using the full right-acyclic comparison. For lower term bound n, total degree m>=n stabilizes by page m-n+2 with at most m-n+1 graded pieces.
claims.hypotheses: Actual bounded-below resolutions; commuting double-complex squares and total sign d_1+(-1)^p d_2; for composition A and B have enough injectives and each F(I) has canonical G(F(I))[0]->RG(F(I)[0]) invertible.

claims.original_statement: A bounded-below complex has a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution when the abelian category has enough injectives.
claims.proved_statement: The boundary resolutions for p>=n+1 and cohomology resolutions for p>=n may be prescribed simultaneously. The actual horizontal differential is the quotient-to-boundary, inclusion-to-cycle, inclusion-to-term composite. The boundary resolution at n must be zero when earlier columns are zero.
claims.hypotheses: K^p=0 for p<n; the prescribed injective resolutions vanish in vertical degrees below zero. No additional global enough-injectives hypothesis once these are supplied.

claims.original_statement: Bounded-below filtered complexes admit strict monomorphic filtered injective resolutions with each output filtration finite.
claims.proved_statement: If K^p has filtration interval [a_p,b_p] and is zero below N, the output in degree m has interval [min_{N<=p<=m}a_p,max_{N<=p<=m}b_p] and remains zero below N. With functorial injective embeddings and a fixed interval [a,b], the construction is functorial and retains both bounds. Its chain-level additivity defect has a filtered homotopy relative to K.
claims.hypotheses: Enough injectives for the chosen varying-window construction; functorial injective embeddings for fixed-window functoriality. All filtrations finite; bounded below term complex. A variable objectwise choice of interval is not asserted to define a functor.

claims.original_statement: A strict short exact sequence of filtered objects has a compatible termwise split sequence of injective resolutions retaining both given outer resolutions.
claims.proved_statement: The construction works for degreewise strict short exact sequences of bounded-below filtered complexes, retaining both prescribed filtered injective resolutions even when their augmentation maps are not monomorphic. The actual middle map has off-diagonal homotopy h and preserves common outer bounds.
claims.hypotheses: Degreewise strict exact source sequence, given filtered quasi-isomorphisms to bounded-below filtered injective complexes. No additional global enough-injectives hypothesis once these exist.

claims.original_statement: Left exact T acts on finite filtrations by T(F^p A); arbitrary additive T is extended on split filtered injectives to define RT.
claims.proved_statement: Every additive T acts on all finite filtered objects with F^p T_im(A)=im(T(F^p A)->T(A)). This is additive, preserves finite filtration intervals, and its right derived functor is the source RT=T_ext j, with the actual comparison induced by the resolution map.
claims.hypotheses: A,B abelian and T additive; enough injectives in A for the bounded-below derived statement. No preservation of monomorphisms is assumed.

claims.original_statement: Finite term filtrations imply boundedness, convergence, and finite cohomology filtrations.
claims.proved_statement: For C^m supported in filtration interval [a_m,b_m], E_r^{p,m-p} has stabilized once r>=max(1,b_(m+1)-p+1,p-a_(m-1)+1). A full degree m stabilizes by max(1,b_(m+1)-a_m+1,b_m-a_(m-1)+1), with at most b_m-a_m+1 graded pieces. A common interval [a,b] gives page b-a+1 even without a bound on complex degrees.
claims.hypotheses: An abelian category and finite decreasing exhaustive separated filtration on each actual term. Adjacent-degree bounds are retained. Derived receiving bounds use the PART11 bounded-below resolution construction.

claims.original_statement: The product vanishes exactly when a compatible extension diagram exists.
claims.proved_statement: The fiber of Ext^1(Zprime,A) to Ext^1(B,A) over the first extension class is empty exactly when the product is nonzero; otherwise it is a torsor under Ext^1(C,A)/im(Hom(B,A) to Ext^1(C,A)).
claims.hypotheses: An abelian category and the two specified short exact sequences. No enough-injective or enough-projective assumption.
claims.limits: Classifies middle-row extension classes admitting a compatibility isomorphism; it does not fix the isomorphism as part of the classification.

claims.original_statement: All Ext^p(H^r K,H^s K) vanish for p>=2 and r>s.
claims.proved_statement: Only Ext^(r-s+1)(H^r K,H^s K)=0 for r>s is needed for splitting. The actual truncation boundary is the precise stage obstruction. Identity-on-cohomology splittings form a torsor under 1+N, where N is the nilpotent ideal with entries Ext^(r-s)(H^r K,H^s K), r>s; when these entries vanish the splitting is unique.
claims.hypotheses: K has bounded cohomology in an abelian category, with the displayed degree-specific vanishing for existence.

claims.original_statement: Compatible split resolution stages are bounded above, or dually bounded below.
claims.proved_statement: Stages can be chosen with P_n^r=0 for r>n, and dually I_n^r=0 for r<-n. A surjective cone resolution gives P_(n+1)=P_n direct-sum Q with differential [[dP,-v],[0,dQ]], augmentation (a,u), and an exact identity of its cone with C(q), so compatibility and surjectivity hold on chain maps without an extra disk.
claims.hypotheses: An abelian category and a zero-containing finite-sum-closed class surjecting onto every object; the exact opposite hypotheses for the inverse system.
claims.limits: No functorial choice of all resolutions or general inverse-limit comparison is asserted.

claims.original_statement: The existence criterion assumes right exactness and preservation of all sequential colimits by F.
claims.proved_statement: It suffices that F is additive, preserves countable coproducts, and takes bounded above acyclic complexes of P objects to acyclic complexes; both abelian categories still have exact sequential colimits. The same strict systems compute LF on the entire unbounded derived category, with comparisons proved compatible at every stage.
claims.hypotheses: The stated P covering and finite-sum hypotheses, exact sequential colimits in A and B, and the specified additive F assumptions.
claims.example: For abelian groups F(M)=M[ell] with P free, LF=0 although F is not right exact.
claims.limits: No assertion H^0 LF(M)=F(M) without right exactness, and no removal of exact sequential colimits.

claims.original_statement: An existing termwise inverse limit of K-injectives with degreewise split-surjective transitions is K-injective.
claims.proved_statement: For arbitrary transitions and each acyclic M, Hom_K(M,lim I_n) is naturally the kernel of C^1(Z_n^-1) to C^1(D_n^-1), where D_n is the full Hom complex, Z its cycles and C^1 the cokernel of the explicit product difference map. Mittag-Leffler in degree -2 of D_n suffices for K-injectivity.
claims.hypotheses: An abelian category, a countable tower of K-injectives, and existence of its termwise limit; the sufficient criterion is imposed for every acyclic M.
claims.example: The nonsurjective tower I_0 direct-sum J with transitions diag(id,0) has limit I_0 and satisfies the criterion.
claims.limits: No arbitrary inverse-limit exactness and no unproved claim that a compatible map from K to this limit is a quasi-isomorphism.

claims.original_statement: The replacement process eventually stabilizes in every degree.
claims.proved_statement: After the corrected initial splice, at most N_m=sum of d_j over positive d_j with j+d_j at least m elementary replacements affect any degree at least m. The actual eventual terms, differentials and finite composite maps give the quasi-isomorphic acyclic replacement without an infinite-colimit assumption.
claims.hypotheses: The source dimension axioms and far-left limit, with the finite dimensions d_j taken after the initial splice.
claims.limits: The bound is for tail-affecting elementary replacements after the initial splice, not a global finite bound on the infinite algorithm.

claims.original_statement: Finite cohomological dimension gives the listed canonical truncation isomorphisms and support intervals.
claims.proved_statement: For n at least 1, H^i RF(E) is determined by the canonical window [i-n+1,i] with its extension data; the dual LF window is [i,i+n-1]. The adjacent upper and lower truncation maps have the stated monomorphism and epimorphism endpoints.
claims.hypotheses: Exactly the source enough-acyclics and R^n F=0 hypotheses, or their right-exact left-derived dual; n=0 is the zero-functor case.
claims.limits: A truncation window retains its extension data; a list of individual cohomology objects does not determine the answer.

claims.original_statement: For an object whose Hom functor preserves all countable sums, maps to a sequential homotopy colimit form the colimit of the stage Hom groups.
claims.proved_statement: For any object P and this sequence, write A_r for the direct sum of stage Hom groups, B_r=Hom(P,S[r]), Q_r=B_r/A_r, d_r induced by u[r] and e_r its quotient map. The comparison kernel is coker(ker d_0 to ker e_0), and its cokernel lies in the exact sequence 0 to coker e_0 to coker lambda to ker d_1 to 0. These give the exact bijectivity criterion and weaker sufficient conditions.
